sources.entry: app-menu - The missing Applications Menu for macOS.

summary.one_liner: app-menu is a macOS menu bar utility that adds an Applications menu listing installed apps, as a replacement for the missing system Applications menu.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes app-menu as the missing Applications Menu for macOS. It shows a menu of applications on the Mac. By default it lists apps in the system Applications folder. To also list apps in the user's ~/Applications folder, the user must grant the app access to that directory in the app's Settings. A Refresh item in the menu reloads the application list after access is granted. It can be installed through Homebrew Cask or by downloading a DMG from GitHub Releases. The README lists compatibility with macOS Tahoe (26.x), Sequoia (15.x), Sonoma (14.x) and Ventura (13.x). Details beyond this are not covered in the README.
use_cases: launch installed mac apps from a menu bar
browse applications without the Dock or Launchpad
install a mac menu bar app via Homebrew
replace a missing Applications menu on macOS
how_to_run: Alternatively: download ApplicationMenu.dmg from GitHub Releases
Open the DMG and drag ApplicationMenu into the Applications folder
Open Settings in the app and grant access to ~/Applications
Click Refresh in the menu to reload the applications list
notable: Lists user ~/Applications apps once the user grants folder access in Settings
Installable via a Homebrew tap and cask, or manually from a DMG
Covers macOS 13 Ventura through macOS 26 Tahoe according to the README
caveats: Apps in ~/Applications are only listed after the user grants folder access and refreshes
README gives no details on implementation language or features beyond the basic menu
Listed under menubar apps in an awesome-style list, but the README itself does not describe build or source requirements
